-- Luau's experimental `if local` / `while local` / `const` syntax (a friend's case). The binding
-- lives only in the then-branch or loop body, so an outer variable with the same name has to
-- stay visible in the else-branch, and every loop iteration gets a fresh local for closures.
do
	const t = {1, 2, 3}
	while local v = table.remove(t) do
		print(v, #t)
	end
end
do
	local items = {"a", "b", false, "c"}
	local i = 0
	local function nextItem()
		i += 1
		return items[i]
	end
	-- false ends the loop just like nil
	while const item = nextItem() do
		print("item", item)
	end
	print("stopped at", i)
end
do
	local fns = {}
	local queue = {10, 20, 30}
	while local n = table.remove(queue, 1) do
		table.insert(fns, function()
			return n
		end)
	end
	print(fns[1](), fns[2](), fns[3]())
end
do
	local x = "outer"
	if local x = nil then
		print("then", x)
	else
		print("else", x)
	end
	if local x = "inner" then
		print("then", x)
	end
	print("after", x)
end
do
	local function classify(s)
		if local n: number? = tonumber(s) then
			return "number " .. n * 2
		elseif local first = string.match(s, "^%a+") then
			return "word " .. first
		elseif const sym = string.match(s, "^%p") then
			return "symbol " .. sym
		else
			return "other"
		end
	end
	print(classify("21"), classify("hello world"), classify("!?"), classify("  "))
end
do
	local function lookup(t, k)
		return if local v = t[k] then v .. "!" else "missing"
	end
	local map = {a = "x", b = "y"}
	print(lookup(map, "a"), lookup(map, "z"))
	const limit = 3
	local count = 0
	while local v = count < limit and count do
		count = v + 1
	end
	print("count", count)
end

-- locals that are written inside a loop and read after it, or in a repeat's condition
do
	local function scan(s)
		local depth, out = 0, {}
		local i = 1
		while i <= #s do
			local c = string.sub(s, i, i)
			if c == "(" then
				depth += 1
			elseif c == ")" then
				depth -= 1
				if depth < 0 then
					return "unbalanced at " .. i
				end
			elseif c == "x" and depth == 0 then
				table.insert(out, i)
			else
				i += 1
				continue
			end
			i += 1
		end
		if depth ~= 0 then
			return "open"
		end
		return table.concat(out, ",")
	end
	print(scan("x(x)x"), scan("(()"), scan("())x"), scan(""))
end
do
	local fs = {}
	local i = 0
	repeat
		i += 1
		local x = i * 3
		table.insert(fs, function() return x end)
	until x > 10
	local r = {}
	for _, f in fs do table.insert(r, f()) end
	print(table.concat(r, ","))
	local function g(t)
		local n = 0
		repeat
			n += 1
			local v = t[n]
		until v == nil or v < 0
		return n
	end
	print(g({1, 2, -1, 5}), g({}))
end

-- vectors: vector.create with constant arguments folds into a vector constant, which has to come
-- back as something vanilla Luau runs (Roblox spells it Vector3.new, plain Luau doesn't have
-- that), plus vector arithmetic, components and the vector library, which compile to fast calls
local function show(v)
	return string.format("%g,%g,%g", v.x, v.y, v.z)
end

local up = vector.create(0, 1, 0)
local unit = vector.create(1, 1, 1)
print(show(up), show(unit), typeof(up), up == vector.create(0, 1, 0))
print(show(vector.create(-0, 0.5, 1e300)), show(vector.create(1 / 3, 2 ^ 20, -7)))

-- arithmetic with vectors and numbers, and unary minus
local a, b = vector.create(1, 2, 3), vector.create(4, 5, 6)
print(show(a + b), show(a - b), show(a * b), show(b / a), show(a * 2), show(3 / b), show(-a), show(b // a))

-- components, and arguments known only at run time
local n = #"abcd"
local v = vector.create(n, n * 2, n // 3)
print(v.x, v.y, v.z, v.X, v.Y, v.Z)

-- the vector library
print(vector.magnitude(vector.create(3, 4, 0)), show(vector.normalize(vector.create(0, 0, 9))))
print(vector.dot(a, b), show(vector.cross(a, b)), show(vector.floor(vector.create(1.5, -1.5, 2))))
print(show(vector.ceil(vector.create(1.2, -1.2, 0))), show(vector.abs(vector.create(-1, 2, -3))))
print(show(vector.sign(vector.create(-5, 0, 5))), show(vector.clamp(vector.create(5, -5, 0), vector.zero, vector.one)))
print(show(vector.max(a, b, vector.create(9, 0, 0))), show(vector.min(a, b)), vector.angle(vector.create(1, 0, 0), up))
print(show(vector.zero), show(vector.one))

local seen = {}
seen[vector.create(1, 2, 3)] = "found"
print(seen[a], a == vector.create(1, 2, 3), a ~= b)
